title: As for me and my house (Joshua 24:14–15)
hookLine: the old leader says: choose this day whom you'll serve

lines: A LINE OVER THE FRONT DOOR.
cards: Some families hang a line from today's chapter over the front door: "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD." On a plaque it looks like a cozy motto. In the story it ends a hard speech.
Joshua is old, and the text says God has given Israel rest.

He gathers the tribes at Shechem and tells their history back to them: Abraham's father beyond the river, Egypt, the sea, the wilderness, the land under their feet. Then he stops telling the story and asks them to decide.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Now therefore fear the LORD, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the LORD."
That flood isn't Noah's. In the King James it means the river: verse two says Abraham's father Terah lived on the other side of it.

teach.h: NOT WHETHER YOU SERVE, BUT WHOM.
teach.b: Then verse fifteen: "choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."
Notice three things. First, serve keeps coming back. Israel came out of the house of bondage, out of serving Pharaoh.
The question was never whether they'd serve. It was whom. Second, the choice is specific: the old gods of the family, or the local gods of the neighbors.
The pull of the past, and the pull of fitting in. Third, Joshua decides for his own house in the same breath as the question.
He doesn't wait for a vote. The people answer: "God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods."
Then Joshua startles them: "Ye cannot serve the LORD: for he is an holy God."

teach.h: AS FOR ME AND MY HOUSE.
teach.b: He presses, and they answer again, "Nay; but we will serve the LORD." Only then does he write it in a book and set up a great stone under an oak, a witness that has heard every word.

how: Some Christian families hang Joshua 24:15 in their homes, over a door or in the kitchen, as a statement of what their household serves.

games.q: you're one of the tribes at Shechem. Joshua says: choose this day whom you'll serve. you answer that you'll serve the LORD. what does Joshua say back?
o: ye cannot serve the LORD: for he is an holy God.
games.why: he presses them hard (24:19), and they answer again: "Nay; but we will serve the LORD." only then does he write it down and set up the stone.

practice: Your household might be family, roommates, or just you and a cat.

Let an ordinary week pass in front of you, meals, screens, mornings, money, and ask what your home actually serves; then choose one small thing it will do on purpose, like a meal without phones or a word of thanks at dinner.
If you pray, offer that choice to God.
